exact_statement: For the actual parity/band selector on n=16r^2 fair data bits, r>=1, with band sign g positive at counts <=n/2-r or >=n/2+r, and independent selector probability epsilon in (0,1/2], let F be parity when C=0 and g when C=1. Let a=2(2r-1)Pr[Bin(n-1,1/2)=n/2-r]/(n-1), m=2epsilon a, V=4(1-epsilon)+epsilon E Z_g^2-4epsilon^2a^2 for the actual integer data-pair profile. The complete mean-refunded pair bill is L_kappa=binom(n,2)kappa(m)V/4, and exact signed pair residual is Q_pair=binom(n,2)h(m)/4, where kappa(m)=2m ln(1/m)/(1-m), h(m)=m^2 ln(1/m^2). With D=I-Var, L_kappa/D>=epsilon(1-epsilon)ln((n-1)/(4epsilon))/6, while 0<=Q_pair/D<=10epsilon^2 ln((n-1)/(4epsilon))/n. On epsilon=1/k,r=2^(k^2),k>=2, the former is >=k ln2/6 and diverges while the latter tends to zero. Ordinary H/I<=2+2/n, so this is a ledger obstruction, not a FEI disproof. For any fixed n>=1 and Boolean branch g on fair data, at the same parity-selector endpoint write mu=Eg,t=E[g parity], b_T=ghat(T)-1_{T=full}, J=sum_all_data_T b_T^2 ln(4/b_T^2), Z=1-t^2-mu^2, B=sum_nonempty_T_not_full h(ghat(T))-J-3(1-t)^2. Then corrected natural E=epsilon[2(1-t)+J]+2Z epsilon^2 ln(1/epsilon)+B epsilon^2+O_g,n(epsilon^3), and exact D=n-1+epsilon[I(g)-n+2-2t]-epsilon^2[2-2t-mu^2]. At n>=2 the limiting unit atom has positive deficit n-1. At n=1 the four branches yield respectively E=D=0 for g=parity, E/D->1 for g=-parity and E/D->2+4ln2 for constant branches, with ratios here in natural units. There is no claim of a bounded selected whole-set reference or universal FEI theorem.

exact_statement: For an actual Boolean pair mixed profile Z_S with mean m and 0<|m|<1, the smallest universally valid nonnegative variance multiplier depending only on the mean is kappa(|m|)=2|m|ln(1/|m|)/(1-|m|): h(m)<=kappa(|m|)Var(Z_S), h(m)=m^2ln(1/m^2), and every real mean in this interval is attained sharply by the actual AND3 sign with the pair selected and controller probability |m| (negate for negative means). Set kappa(0)=0 and charge no positive residual at |m|>=1. The sum-all-pairs strict-superset packet bill L_kappa=sum_{|S|=2,0<|m_S|<1}kappa(|m_S|)sum_{T strictly containing S}P_F(T) has no finite universal root-deficit price. For every integer r>=1 let n=16r^2 fair data bits, g=+1 if their one-count N<=n/2-r or N>=n/2+r and -1 otherwise; a fresh fair selector chooses parity (-1)^N or g. This is an actual Boolean sign F. Every data-pair mixed-profile mean equals a=2(2r-1)Pr[Bin(n-1,1/2)=n/2-r]/(n-1), with 1/[8(n-1)]<=a<=2/(n-1). Two actual full-data Fourier packets have combined mass>=1/2 and strictly contain every data pair. Hence L_kappa(F)>=n ln((n-1)/2)/16 and L_kappa(F)/Delta(F)>=ln((n-1)/2)/24 tends to infinity, using Delta(F)<=n+1<=3n/2. Any other nonnegative mean-only multiplier valid for all actual Boolean pair profiles is at least kappa and fails the same all-pairs universal price. Nonetheless ordinary H(F)/I(F)<=2+2/n. This is a mean-only variance-ledger obstruction, not an FEI disproof or a refutation of exact signed residuals, selected pairs, full profile laws or joint complete-reference allocation.
